# FloodNav Phase 1 — Consolidated Plan (Backend + Frontend)

**Consolidates:** the CEO-approved backend scope plan (`~/.gstack/projects/3plus1wheels-airflow_new/ceo-plans/2026-08-07-floodnav-phase1-core-pipeline.md`, generated by `/plan-ceo-review` on 2026-08-07, hardened by `/plan-eng-review`) and the frontend URD (`artifacts/[20260714]URD_RoutingMapApp_Wireframe2a.md`, v4.2, hardened by `/plan-design-review` + `/plan-eng-review`). Merged 2026-09-04 because the two documents drifted from each other three separate times during review (GeoJSON-vs-raster data source, TimescaleDB consumer status, unregistered backend tasks) — one document removes that failure mode going forward. The two original files remain in place with a pointer to this one; this file is authoritative.

**Not folded in:** `airflow_tsm/data/mapping/SW Architecture.md` — the full 12-month target-platform vision (dual-horizon simulation, gauge hot-start, dashboard, mobile app, alerting, Phase 3 partner API). Explicitly out of Phase 1 scope per the CEO plan below; kept separate so this document doesn't read as more in-scope than it is.

## 1. Vision & Context

SW Architecture.md describes the full target FloodNav platform: dual-horizon simulation, gauge hot-start, PostGIS+TimescaleDB+Redis, FastAPI citizen+dashboard API, mobile app, council dashboard, FCM/APNs alerting, Phase-3 partner API. The current codebase (per the now-deleted `ARCHITECTURE_AND_FEATURES.md`) was a single-DAG prototype: Tomorrow.io rain gate → 3Di sim → depth GeoTIFFs → GeoJSON → MinIO, plus a separate floodmap-backend + Leaflet UI doing Valhalla flood-weighted routing off the newest MinIO GeoJSON object.

**Real infra constraints (from domain owner, override the target doc's assumptions):**
- Only ONE 3Di simulation can run at a time — no concurrency. Kills the target doc's constant_cycle/background_cycle-run-independently model as written.
- No gauge/rainfall sensor access — Tomorrow.io rain forecast is the only live input. Gauge-based hot-start is not buildable in Phase 1.
- Depth representation flips vector → raster: GeoTIFF/XYZ tiles are the source of truth; routing cost samples depth via `rasterio` directly against road segments, not via GeoJSON polygon intersection or a polygon-derived PostGIS segment model.
- No background_cycle in Phase 1. Single continuous cycle, duration reduced to 2h.
- Frontend priority: citizen floodmap + routing engine first. Dashboard, mobile histograms, and alerting are explicitly later phases — this is the frontend spec'd in Part B below.

**Dream State Delta:** Phase 1 moves the system from "single fixture-bound DAG with a crude proto-backend" to "a validated, raster-accurate, single-cycle production pipeline with real storage and a citizen-facing floodmap + router" — a meaningful step toward the 12-month ideal, but deliberately stops short of dual-horizon, alerting, and the dashboard. The gap that remains is entirely gated on external constraints (gauge access, 3Di concurrency) or later-phase product surface, not on avoidable scope-cutting.

## 2. Scope Decisions (CEO Review)

| # | Proposal | Effort | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Gauge-failure fallback (prev-cycle value + degraded-cycle logging) | S | N/A | No gauge data exists in Phase 1 at all — moot, not deferred |
| 2 | Pre-sample per-segment depth to PostGIS each cycle (vs. query-time-only rasterio) | M | ACCEPTED | Query-time full-raster rasterio sampling per request will not hold up under concurrent citizen load; pre-sampling once per cycle is the only way route/point queries stay fast |
| 3 | Stand up TimescaleDB now for depth history, even with no Phase 1 consumer | M | ACCEPTED (user override of recommendation) | Recommendation was to defer (zero Phase 1 consumer = premature infra); user chose to build it now to avoid a Phase 2 backfill/migration gap once histogram features start. **Update 2026-09-04: no longer zero-consumer** — see §5 below |

## 3. Accepted Scope (Phase 1)

- Fix fixture-bound depth step: wire real 3Di NetCDF download into `calculate_waterdepth` — **verified stale, dropped** (see T3 below; already fixed by an earlier commit than the audit that flagged it).
- Single continuous 2h-cycle DAG (no background_cycle, no gauge ingestion). 2h figure is driven by 3Di single-model-slot compute budget observed in current runs, not the Tomorrow.io forecast refresh interval — needs a benchmark pass to confirm it holds under the new raster pipeline's added rasterio-sampling step.
- 3Di auth-token expiry: catch the SDK's `ApiException` and branch on `status in (401, 403)` (not a `ThreeDiAuthError` type, which doesn't exist in `threedi-api-client==5.0.5` — confirmed by direct grep during eng review) — skip cycle + serve stale like other failures, but fire a distinct "auth expired, will not self-resolve" alert/log, since unlike a timeout the next cycle will fail identically until the token is rotated.
- Corrupt/truncated raster detection: validate each cycle's `results_3di.nc` and per-timestep depth GeoTIFFs against expected size/NoData-ratio bounds (calibrated from a known-good reference) before writing to PostGIS. If a file is far smaller than expected or has an abnormally high NoData fraction, treat it as a cycle failure (same skip-cycle + serve-stale path as a 3Di timeout), not a silent bad write.
- **Depth pipeline rebuilt around raster (GeoTIFF/XYZ tiles) as source of truth; routing cost sampled via `rasterio` against road segments. Cutover status: ACCEPTED — sampling method resolved.** Method: raster-only, no mixed/polygon fallback. `sample_road_depths.py` densifies each road LineString every ~5m, samples `depth_<ts>.tif` directly via `rasterio.sample.sample_gen` (one raster open per timestep, not per road), takes the **max valid (non-NoData) depth per road per timestep**. Replaces `extract_geojson_full.py` + `merge_geojson.py` + `mapping_geojson.py` as a single task. Cutover is a hard swap, not a feature flag — those three files get deleted once the new task is verified (T9's regression diff, mandatory per the IRON RULE — see §7).
- Scope boundary: Phase 1 concerns **only** `flood_mapping_full`. `flood_forecast_pipeline`, `flood_initial_wl_pipeline`, `initial_wl_dummy_pipeline`, and `manholes_...` are out of scope — no disposition decision is being made for them in Phase 1.
- Out-of-extent segments: any route that would cross a road segment outside the 3Di model's simulated raster extent is **cut off** — the routing/point API returns invalid/no-route rather than routing through unmeasured terrain at any cost. Absence of data must never look like confirmation of safety — enforced as a hard exclusion, not a soft penalty. Implementation: a road with zero valid (non-NoData) samples is excluded from routing entirely; no `depth_status` enum or penalty-cost band needed, just an exclusion check in the routing query.
- PostGIS pre-sampling has an immediate Phase 1 consumer (route/point endpoints ship using it day one) — unlike TimescaleDB's original zero-consumer status, this isn't premature infra, but do not over-provision for a specific QPS number; no citizen load has been measured yet, so size it minimally and revisit if real usage demands more.
- **PostGIS:** per-segment depth pre-sampled and written once per cycle. Writes are transactional (new-cycle write completes before old-cycle rows are replaced); route/point queries always read the last fully-written cycle, never a partial write. If a cycle's 3Di run fails outright, PostGIS is left untouched and queries continue serving the last-good cycle's data with a staleness flag. Per-cycle write is **UPSERT** (`INSERT...ON CONFLICT`) keyed by `way_id`, not DELETE+INSERT, to avoid GIST index bloat under continuous ~2h-cycle writes. Requires `CREATE EXTENSION postgis` + a geometry column + GIST index — today's DB has no PostGIS extension enabled at all despite the "PostGIS" naming (confirmed: `create_geojson_tables.py:26-42` uses plain JSONB), needed to support `GET /flood/points`'s radius query.
- **TimescaleDB:** depth history written every cycle starting now. **No longer zero-consumer as of 2026-09-04** — the routing frontend's depth-forecast chart (Part B, REQ-DET-001) reads the immediately-prior timestep from TimescaleDB for its "-30" bar, ahead of the originally-assumed Phase 2 histogram consumer. **Retention urgency raised**: no TTL/rollup policy is defined yet; originally flagged as a Phase 1 exit TODO (before Phase 2 histogram work), now that a real reader exists in Phase 1 itself, unbounded per-cycle growth directly grows a table an active query pattern reads from. **Set retention before REQ-DET-001 ships, not before Phase 2.**
- **REST surface:** extend existing `floodmap-backend` (port 8010) to read from PostGIS/raster instead of newest-MinIO-GeoJSON polling — no new FastAPI service in Phase 1 (avoids a duplicate HTTP service; existing backend already does the job).
- **Frontend:** citizen floodmap (raster tile visualization) + routing engine UI only — fully spec'd in Part B below.

## 4. What Already Exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- 3Di orchestration (`create_simulation.py`), including bounded-polling (`monitor_simulation`: timeout + exponential backoff + max consecutive-error cap) — already supports cold-start and saved-state hot-start.
- Depth GeoTIFF generation (`calculate_depth.py`, `threedidepth.calculate_waterdepth()`) — this is Phase 1's raster source (with additive fixes from T13/T15 below, not logic changes).
- NetCDF-to-depth wiring (`netcdf_input.py`) — already pulls the real downloaded file via XCom, not a fixture.
- Valhalla flood-weighted routing (already running, `linear_cost_factors` active) — re-weighting source changes from GeoJSON-derived to PostGIS-derived, routing itself is reused.
- `floodmap-backend` (port 8010) — extended in place rather than replaced by a new FastAPI service.
- `flood_forecast_state_test_dag.py` — existing manual-trigger test harness; the required validation path for any `calculate_depth.py` change (a past incident made direct production-DAG edits unsafe — see `feedback-calculate-depth-fragility`).
- `airflow_tsm/test/` (`test_flood_rain_gate.py`, `test_minio_bucket_routing.py`, `test_model_netcdf_input.py`) — existing unittest suite for rain-gate and netcdf-input paths.
- **(Frontend, Part B)** Leaflet map instance, map-click point-picking, and Photon place-search integration — already implemented in `frontend/app.js`. Existing Bike/Truck Valhalla costing profiles reused as-is.
- **(Frontend, Part B)** `tests/test_point_depth.js` + `frontend/point_depth.js` — the pure-function/`node:test` pattern all new frontend test files (Part B §Test Plan) follow.
- `scripts/run_route_tests.py` + `scripts/flood_utils.py` — existing Python route-testing harness against `requests/`/`responses/` fixtures.

## 5. NOT in Scope

- Gauge network ingestion + hot-start — blocked on sensor access, not a build decision.
- Dual-horizon (background_cycle 24h simulation) — blocked on single-3Di-slot constraint; needs either a second 3Di model/account or a scheduling strategy that time-shares the one slot.
- Institution/route depth histograms, city council dashboard, mobile app, FCM/APNs alerting, in-app poll fallback — explicitly Phase 2/3.
- Phase 3 ride-hailing partner API (`/partner/flood/points`, MVT tile worker, partner auth).
- Rate limiting on citizen endpoints (T11) — deferred pre-launch, required before any public rollout.
- `flood_initial_wl_pipeline`, `flood_forecast_pipeline`, and other DAGs — Phase 1 concerns only `flood_mapping_full`.
- **(Frontend, Part B)** Dark mode, keyboard-driven arbitrary-point map picking, `--alert-*` tokens (reserved for a future dashboard/alerting surface), redesigning `app.js`'s module structure, adopting an E2E/browser test framework, and the strategic question of whether this much UI polish is warranted before the backend ships (a CEO-review-level question, flagged not acted on).

## A2. PR Staging

Step 0 complexity check tripped during eng review (10-12 files, 2 new datastores in one plan) — split into 3 staged PRs:

- **PR1 — failure-taxonomy hardening** (T4, T12, T13, T14, T15, E2): 5-6 files, no new infra, independently testable via `flood_forecast_state_test_dag.py`.
- **PR2 — raster cutover** (T1, T5, T6, T9, E3, E4): new `sample_road_depths.py` + way-ID-keyed PostGIS schema, hard-deletes 3 old files once T9's regression diff passes. T8 (PR3) blocked on this PR being **merged**, not just branched.
- **PR3 — TimescaleDB stand-up + backend rewrite** (T7, T8, T10, E5, E6): the re-scoped backend rewrite, now also gating T16/T17/T18 (frontend-driven backend tasks added below).

**Worktree parallelization:** Lane A: PR1 (independent). Lane B: PR2 (waits on PR1 merge for `db_config.py`). Lane C: PR3 (waits on PR2 merge for T6 schema) → then T16 → T17 → T18 sequentially (all touch `floodmap-backend`). Sequential dependency chain, not parallelizable across worktrees — each stage's DB layer depends on the prior stage's schema/config decisions.

## A3. Error & Rescue Registry

| Method/Codepath | Exception | Rescued? | Rescue Action | User Sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3Di trigger/poll | `ThreeDiTimeoutError`, crash/shut_down | Y | Skip cycle, serve last-good (T4) | Staleness flag |
| 3Di trigger/poll | `ApiException.status in (401,403)` | Y (T4, re-scoped) | Skip cycle + distinct "won't self-resolve" alert | Distinguishable from a timeout |
| 3Di trigger/poll failure (any) | `AirflowSkipException` cascade | Y (T14) | Distinct failure signal vs. dry-cycle skip | Distinguishable in Airflow UI |
| Per-timestep depth calc | Exception inside `calculate_waterdepth` | Y (T13) | Task fails instead of reporting partial success | Clear failure, not silent partial data |
| rasterio read | `RasterioIOError` / undersized/high-NoData file | Y (T4) | Treat as cycle failure, skip write, serve stale | Staleness flag |
| Timestamp-parse failure on depth tif | (no exception, returns None) | Y (T15) | File renamed correctly, no orphan | N/A |
| PostGIS pre-sample write | `OperationalError` / `IntegrityError` | Y (transactional UPSERT, T6) | New-cycle write completes before old rows replaced | Last-good cycle, no partial state |
| TimescaleDB history write | `OperationalError` | Y | Log + continue | Nothing (transparent) |
| Route/point query, out-of-extent segment | N/A (data gap, not exception) | Y (T6) | Hard exclusion — no route through unmeasured terrain | Invalid/no-route response |
| `sample_road_depths.py` road w/ zero valid samples | Corrupt raster OR genuinely dry — ambiguous cause | Partial (T9 diffs happy path; E6 metric surfaces the rate) | T4 upstream detection; E6 metric downstream | Road silently excluded; exclusion-rate spike now visible via E6 |
| `server.py` rewrite (T8) | PostGIS query returns no matching way_id for a route's matched roads | N — new adapter has zero tests today, E7 adds them | Not yet designed | **Flagged for T8 implementation to resolve explicitly** (fall back to no-cost, or exclude the road?) |

**Critical gaps:** none unresolved as of the last eng review — the one live risk (T5/T9 corrupt-vs-dry ambiguity) has a mitigating metric (E6); the `server.py` no-match case is flagged for explicit resolution during T8, not silently assumed.

# Part B: Frontend Requirements (URD)

**User Requirements Document — Flood-Aware Routing Map App (Wireframe 2a).** Document version 4.2, last revised 2026-09-04.

## B1. Purpose

The Flood-Aware Routing Map App gives citizens and stakeholder viewers a Google-Maps-style interface — built on wireframe 2a's layout — for finding routes that account for real-time and forecast flood depth in Hanoi. It re-skins the existing, already-functional floodmap-frontend (Leaflet + Valhalla + flood data) into wireframe 2a's split-panel-plus-layer-strip design, adds place-name search, and extends vehicle costing to match the fuller vehicle picker the wireframe calls for. The tool runs continuously and is demonstrated to stakeholders on demand — it is not a public-facing product at this stage.

## B2. Users

**Primary:** Citizen drivers/riders (motorbike, car, truck operators seeking flood-aware directions); TECOTEC/NAWAPI project team (building, testing, operating the app).
**Secondary:** Stakeholder viewers (government/NAWAPI/MAE representatives viewing scheduled demos — view-only, no distinct UI); backend/infrastructure owners (responsible for floodmap-backend, Valhalla, and the data services this app depends on).

## B3. Functional Requirements

*Priority Legend: M = Must Have, S = Should Have, L = Could Have*

### B3.1 Map & Flood Layer

**REQ-MAP-001 — Display base map with pan/zoom (Must).** The system shall display a Leaflet-based map (reusing the existing floodmap-frontend map instance) covering the Hanoi service area, supporting standard pan and zoom interaction. Always-on base layer, not user-toggleable.
*Acceptance:* Map loads and centers on Hanoi by default. Pan/zoom work via mouse, touch, and keyboard.

**REQ-MAP-002 — Toggle flood data layers via a single "Flood" control (Must).** One "Flood" icon in the bottom-right layer strip; selecting it opens the Flood layer. **Data source: raster depth tiles (GeoTIFF/XYZ) rendered from the per-cycle 3Di output via `floodmap-backend`, per Part A's raster-only cutover — not flood_timestamp.geojson from MinIO, which the backend has moved off of.** When the layer is sourced from the scenario library rather than a live 3Di run, the Flood icon carries the `--scenario-library` indicator so viewers don't mistake replayed data for a live simulation.
*Acceptance:* Clicking Flood opens the layer. `--scenario-library` indicator visible only when scenario data is active.

**REQ-MAP-003 — Auto-activate flood layer when a model run is triggered (Must).** Auto-activates the moment a 3Di model run triggers; stays on the base layer with Flood inactive if none has triggered. Manual override via REQ-MAP-002 always available. While a triggered run is in storm-mode (elevated trigger frequency per the pipeline's storm-mode logic), a `--storm-mode` banner surfaces near the layer strip.
*Acceptance:* Layer activates within one refresh cycle of a trigger event; defaults inactive with no trigger; manual toggle overrides until next trigger/reload; storm-mode banner tracks backend state exactly.

**REQ-MAP-004 — Render flood depth using the standardized blue depth scale (Must).** Flood raster-tile fill and depth-forecast chart bars (REQ-DET-001) use a monochromatic blue scale in 20cm bands (0–20/20–40/40–60/60–80/80–100/>100cm) — raw magnitude only. Route/segment safety status uses the separate `--seg-*` tokens instead; never conflate the two. **Data source: pre-sampled per-segment depth (PostGIS, Part A) for routes/segments, and per-cycle raster tiles for the map layer — not flood_timestamp.geojson from MinIO.** Exact values in §B6 Design Tokens — a previously circulated token file used a green→maroon severity gradient in error; §B6 supersedes it.
*Acceptance:* Raster-tile fill uses only the seven §B6 blue/gray shades, correctly banded. No flood-magnitude element uses red/amber/green. Route/segment indicators visibly distinct from the depth scale.

**REQ-MAP-005 — Serve flood raster as an XYZ tile pyramid (Must, backend scope — Part A T17).** `floodmap-backend` serves each cycle's flood-depth GeoTIFF as a standard XYZ tile endpoint (titiler/rio-tiler or pre-cut tiles), not a single full-resolution image. Frontend consumes via Leaflet's `L.tileLayer`, not `L.imageOverlay`. If the tile endpoint is unavailable/times out, it serves the last successfully-generated tile set instead of erroring, mirroring REQ-REL-001.
*Acceptance:* Tile requests scoped to viewport/zoom, not one full-area image per cycle. No visible pan/zoom degradation as extent/resolution grows. Tiles refresh on the 30s cadence without a full-layer reload. Endpoint failure falls back to last-good tiles, no broken placeholders.

### B3.2 Search & Location Input

**REQ-SRCH-001 — Pick origin/destination by clicking the map (Must).** Reuses existing map-click point-picking; baseline input, independent of search. **Mouse/touch-only for this release — no keyboard equivalent.** Keyboard-only users complete selection via place-name search (REQ-SRCH-002) instead; an accepted, documented limitation, not a WCAG gap, since search remains fully keyboard-operable.
*Acceptance:* Click sets the active field, marker appears, works even if search is down.

**REQ-SRCH-002 — Search origin/destination by place name (Must).** Pill-shaped search bar, placeholder "Search a place or address," top-left. Stays a compact pill until clicked. On click (≥768px viewport), expands into a **fixed 340px panel** — matching the Route Results/Detail panel (REQ-RTE-001) for consistent panel width — with the search bar embedded at top. Below 768px, panel becomes full viewport width (REQ-RES-001). On focus+input, calls Photon and renders an autocomplete dropdown (REQ-SRCH-004). Degrades gracefully to map-click if geocoding is unavailable/slow.
*Acceptance:* Pill by default; click opens 340px panel (full-width <768px); selecting a result sets field + marker; geocoding failure still allows map-click completion.

**REQ-SRCH-003 — Display data source and freshness status (Must).** Displays "update: now or _ minutes before" based on newest-file injection time. Past the pipeline's overdue threshold, the badge switches to `--stale-banner` styling (brown) rather than only being distinguishable by reading the minute count.
*Acceptance:* Badge updates each refresh cycle; `--stale-banner` styling only past the overdue threshold, neutral style below it.

**REQ-SRCH-004 — Autocomplete search results (Must, PIC: Alice).** Dropdown activates on the first typed character; each row shows name + address; up to 5 results. While the Photon request is in flight, shows a small inline spinner (§B7) rather than an empty dropdown.
*Acceptance:* 1 character triggers a call and opens the dropdown; max 5 rows; spinner visible for the request's duration.

**REQ-SRCH-005 — Select a location via map pin, then route to it (Must).** Any tapped point gets a red pin + popup (current water depth + "Direction" button). Tapping "Direction" transforms the search bar into the Route Results panel (REQ-RTE-001) with destination pre-filled; origin ready for input.
*Acceptance:* Tap places pin; popup shows depth + button; "Direction" opens Route Results with destination pre-filled, origin empty.

**REQ-SRCH-006 — Select a location via search, then route to it (Must).** Searching and selecting a place shows depth + a "Get directions" button in the search panel; tapping it opens Route Results with destination pre-filled.
*Acceptance:* Same shape as REQ-SRCH-005 via the search path.

### B3.3 Vehicle Mode & Costing

**REQ-VEH-001 — Select vehicle mode: Car / Bike / Transit / Walk (Must).** Four top-level mode icons in a horizontal row; selected icon shows travel time ("Car 13m"); switching modes triggers a new routing request. Car carries a ▾ opening the sub-profile dropdown (REQ-VEH-002). Bike reuses the existing motor-scooter costing profile (20cm threshold). Transit/Walk have no existing backend costing today — gated on REQ-VEH-003 (Part A, T16).
*Acceptance:* All 4 icons always visible/selectable; selected icon shows travel time once computed; switching updates cards/polylines/ETA; Car shows ▾ and opens the dropdown; Bike returns routes immediately; Transit/Walk functional once T16 lands.

**REQ-VEH-002 — Select a Car sub-profile: Sedan / SUV / Truck (Should).** Dropdown under Car lists Sedan (25cm), SUV (30cm), Truck (reuses existing 50cm profile). Selecting re-runs the route request with that threshold; selection persists while Car is active.
*Acceptance:* Dropdown has exactly 3 options; Truck works immediately; Sedan/SUV enabled once T16 lands; selected label persists.

**REQ-VEH-003 — Extend routing cost model for Transit, Walk, Sedan, SUV (Should — this is Part A T16, tracked there, referenced here for UI gating).** Backend adds Sedan/SUV as distinct Valhalla profiles under Car, and Transit/Walk as new top-level modes (both 40cm). Truck UI moves from top-level tab to the Car dropdown. Not part of the frontend build; gates the Sedan/SUV portion of REQ-VEH-002 and all of Transit/Walk in REQ-VEH-001.
*Acceptance:* See Part A T16.

### B3.4 Route Results

**REQ-RTE-001 — Display route alternatives with ETA, distance, and average depth (Must).** Left panel (fixed 340px ≥768px; full width below, REQ-RES-001) with origin/destination inputs + route cards; map on the right with color-coded polylines + layer strip. Cards from `GET /flood/route/forecast`: route name (via street), ETA, distance, average depth, status line, "See details ▸". Card count is dynamic (typically 1-3), never hardcoded. Copy never implies independent optimization for detour-variant alternatives. While in flight, shows skeleton route cards (§B7) instead of a blank panel.
*Acceptance:* Renders 1-N results correctly including the zero-route empty state (REQ-RTE-003); figures match the API; skeleton cards visible for the request duration.

**REQ-RTE-002 — Color-code each route by safety status (Must).** Card/polyline color reflects the worst-segment `--seg-*` state. **Passable/pre-closure/impassable is computed client-side** by comparing max depth against the active vehicle's unsafe threshold — **returned by the route API response, not hardcoded client-side** (avoids frontend/backend drift). Backend doesn't hard-block by default (`FLOOD_USE_HARD_EXCLUDES=false`), so this classification is required. **Draining is computed backend-side** (Part A T18): the backend compares each segment's consecutive forecast timesteps and returns a `draining: boolean` flag; the frontend reads it rather than re-deriving it. Green (<70% threshold), amber (70-100%), red (≥100%, backend's `crosses_threshold`), blue (`draining:true`, never on a segment also classified impassable).
*Acceptance:* Colors match API-supplied threshold classification and the `draining` flag exactly; never conflated with `--depth-*`; frontend never independently re-derives draining from raw timesteps.

**REQ-RTE-003 — Display a no-safe-route state when applicable (Must).** When the existing 6-hour departure scan finds no safe window, render one explanatory card in place of route cards. Copy follows the non-alarmist register from §B8 User Journey: state the fact plainly, name the next check-in time, avoid dramatized standalone "danger"/"warning" headlines. Worked example: *"No safe route found in the next 6 hours. We'll keep checking — next update in 30 min."*
*Acceptance:* Card appears only when the backend confirms no safe window; standard cards never render alongside it; copy matches the worked-example register.

**REQ-RTE-004 — Open Route Detail from a route card or the map (Should).** Clicking "See details" or tapping the matching polyline both resolve to the same Route Detail view.
*Acceptance:* Both entry points produce an identical Route Detail state.

**REQ-RTE-005 — Return to Home from Route Results or Route Detail (Must).** A back/close affordance (← or ✕) sits in the Route Results and Route Detail panel headers. From Route Detail it returns to Route Results (one level back); a separate close action on Route Results returns to Home, clearing origin/destination/route state.
*Acceptance:* Control always visible in those panel headers; back-from-Detail preserves Results state; close-from-Results clears everything.

### B3.5 Route Detail

**REQ-DET-001 — Display a forward-looking depth forecast chart (Must).** Bars (height ∝ depth, color per §B6 blue scale) + dashed trend line + interactive tooltip. 6 bars at -30/now/+30/+60/+90/+120 (2h window incl. historical -30; 0 if no prior trigger). **This endpoint lives on the existing `floodmap-backend`** (Part A's "no new FastAPI service" decision), querying the PostGIS pre-sampled per-segment table (Part A §3) directly — not GeoJSON. The -30 bar additionally queries the immediately-prior TimescaleDB timestep (Part A §3, now a real consumer). Per REQ-DOC-001's start/stop hysteresis, a fully-stopped simulation means some window bars may fall after the last real cycle — those reuse the last-known value with `--stale-banner` styling, not a false zero or a crash; expected to be rare (the stop condition requires ~5 hours of confirmed drainage first).
*Acceptance:* Correct bar count/window/heights/colors; correct tooltip values on mouse and touch; post-stop bars render last-known + `--stale-banner`, never a false zero or error.

**REQ-DET-003 — Display turn-by-turn steps with per-step depth (Must).** Ordered maneuver list: turn instruction, street, distance, depth; left border colored by depth bucket. Start/end use a pin icon + plain-language descriptor. Per REQ-CALC-002, per-step depth is the length-weighted AVERAGE; whole-route average also shown.
*Acceptance:* Every maneuver rendered correctly; start/end visually distinct; order matches the route; whole-route average visible.

**REQ-DET-004 — Provide a "Start" call-to-action (Could).** "Start" button at the bottom of Route Detail; matches the wireframe's primary CTA styling; clicking focuses/zooms the map to the first step. No live navigation implied.
*Acceptance:* Button present, correct style, correct zoom behavior.

### B3.6 Calculation

**REQ-CALC-001 — Set model output timestep to 1800s (Must, PIC: Alice).** Simulation/model output timestep is 1800 seconds (30 min).
*Acceptance:* Confirmed in simulation config.

**REQ-CALC-002 — Length-Weighted Average Depth Per Turn (Must).** For each maneuver, backend calculates a length-weighted average depth: `avg_depth_cm = Σ(depth_cm_i × overlap_length_i) / Σ(overlap_length_i)` across all intersecting flood-affected road features. Feeds REQ-DET-003 and, after bucketing, `--depth-*` — no color token is itself averaged. Route-level average calculated the same way, weighted by maneuver length.
*Acceptance:* Length-weighted, not max; contribution proportional to overlap length; feeds both the step list and the depth token correctly.

**REQ-CALC-003 — Calculate depth according to a time series (Must, PIC: Alice).** Average depth from origin to destination across a 2h/30min-step forecast window — 5 time blocks (t0/t30/t60/t90/t120). Consecutive time-block deltas per segment feed REQ-RTE-002's draining classification.
*Acceptance:* All 5 time-block values visualized on screen.

### B3.7 Simulation Gating

**REQ-DOC-001 — Gate simulation start/stop on forecast precipitation and drainage state (Must).** Calls Tomorrow.io rainIntensity continuously (2h forecast, 15min timestep). **Start:** while no simulation runs, trigger the moment forecast rainIntensity exceeds 5mm/h in any covered window. **Continue-vs-stop (depth-driven once running, not rain-driven):** each cycle, if rain still exceeds threshold, the simulation continues regardless of depth. If rain drops below threshold, check the persisted per-segment depth history (Part A's PostGIS/TimescaleDB): only stop once **every** segment has read below 0.02m for **10 consecutive cycles** (drainage-confirmed hysteresis) — until then, keep running even with rain below threshold, to keep observing drainage. Once stopped, no new depth output publishes until the next rain-triggered start; last-published output remains, reported per its age (REQ-SRCH-003/REQ-REL-002).
*Acceptance:* Start within one cycle of crossing threshold; continues every cycle rain stays at/above threshold; continues past a below-threshold reading until the 10-cycle drainage hysteresis confirms; stops only then; no new artifacts after stop; start/stop are normal successful DAG runs, never failures.
*(Note: this reconciles/likely supersedes Part A §A5's older "Phase 2: depth-based stop gate" TODO — re-verify that TODO's status once this ships.)*

### B3.8 Navigation

See REQ-RTE-005 above for Route Results/Detail → Home back-navigation.

### B3.9 Responsive Layout

**REQ-RES-001 — Responsive panel behavior below 768px (Must).** All left-panel states (search-expanded, Route Results, Vehicle Mode dropdown, Route Detail) use a fixed 340px width ≥768px. Below 768px, each becomes full viewport width, map revealed beneath via the same expand/collapse interaction. Layer strip and back/close affordance (REQ-RTE-005) remain visible in both layouts. Panel width is the single responsive variable — not a full relayout per breakpoint.
*Acceptance:* Fixed 340px ≥768px; full-width + map hidden below 768px until panel closes; no horizontal scroll 320px→desktop.

## B4. Non-Functional Requirements

| Req. ID | Title | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **REQ-PER-001** | Route Response Time | Route calc returns within 2s P95, consistent with existing Valhalla setup. UI shows the §B7 loading treatment while in flight, never a blank panel. |
| **REQ-PER-002** | Data Refresh Cycle | Flood data cache refreshes at its existing 30s interval without noticeably blocking UI interaction. |
| **REQ-USE-001** | Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA: 44px min tap targets, 4.5:1 text contrast, status distinguishable by icon/pattern beyond color, keyboard navigability (covers all controls except arbitrary map-click, whose keyboard equivalent is search — see REQ-SRCH-001). Primary typeface: Helvetica, Arial fallback (both cover Vietnamese diacritics). |
| **REQ-USE-002** | Localization | All safety-critical/user-facing copy available in Vietnamese, consistent with the existing copy register and REQ-RTE-003's non-alarmist worked example. |
| **REQ-REL-001** | Graceful Degradation | If live flood data is unavailable, fall back to the bundled sample GeoJSON dataset (1,200 LineStrings, two time steps) rather than failing outright. |
| **REQ-REL-002** | Stale Data Handling | Flood data is never silently presented as current when stale — always surfaced via `--stale-banner` past the overdue threshold (REQ-SRCH-003). |
| **REQ-SEC-001** | Deployment Exposure | No public-facing auth required this release. Internal instance shown to stakeholders on demand, no public announcement; stays on a private network as light-touch mitigation (deployment-owner responsibility, not a frontend requirement). |
| **REQ-COM-001** | Design Token Consistency | All depth-magnitude visuals use the single shared `--depth-*` blue scale (§B6, superseding the erroneous non-blue token file); all route/segment indicators use `--seg-*` (incl. `--seg-draining`) — never conflated. `--alert-*` explicitly out of scope (future dashboard surface). `--storm-mode`/`--scenario-library` wired into REQ-MAP-002/003; `--stale-banner` into REQ-SRCH-003/REQ-REL-002. Dark-mode tokens out of scope this release. |

## B5. Interaction States

| FEATURE | LOADING | EMPTY | ERROR | SUCCESS | PARTIAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Route calculation (REQ-RTE-001) | Skeleton route cards (last-known count, or 2 if none); inputs disabled | No prior state — panel shows Home | No-safe-route card (REQ-RTE-003), or on hard API failure: "Couldn't calculate a route — try again" + Retry | Route cards render | N/A — all-or-nothing per request |
| Search autocomplete (REQ-SRCH-004) | Inline spinner; dropdown closed until first result/error | Dropdown closed (no query) | Silently degrades to map-click, no error dialog | Dropdown shows ≤5 results | N/A |
| Flood layer activation (REQ-MAP-003) | Flood icon pulses briefly | N/A — active or inactive | Falls back to bundled sample dataset, no user-facing error | Icon solid active, polygons render | N/A |
| Model trigger / storm-mode (REQ-MAP-003) | N/A | N/A | N/A | `--storm-mode` banner while active | N/A |

## B6. Design Tokens

Canonical values for this app; supersedes any prior circulated token file.

```css
/* ── Flood Depth Magnitude Scale (monochromatic blue, REQ-MAP-004) ───────── */
--depth-0-20:        #E3F2FD;   /* 0–20 cm */
--depth-20-40:       #90CAF9;   /* 20–40 cm */
--depth-40-60:       #42A5F5;   /* 40–60 cm */
--depth-60-80:       #1E88E5;   /* 60–80 cm */
--depth-80-100:      #1565C0;   /* 80–100 cm */
--depth-100-plus:    #0D47A1;   /* >100 cm */
--depth-unknown:     #B0BEC5;   /* No data / stale */

/* ── Alert Level Colors (reserved — out of scope for this app) */
--alert-watch:       #F9A825;
--alert-warning:     #E65100;
--alert-danger:      #B71C1C;
--alert-clear:       #1B5E20;

/* ── Segment State (REQ-RTE-002) ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
--seg-passable:      #4CAF50;
--seg-pre-closure:   #FFB300;   /* Amber — forecast impassable within 1h30 */
--seg-impassable:    #F44336;
--seg-draining:      #29B6F6;   /* Blue — depth falling */

/* ── Surface / UI Chrome ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
/* Light mode (only mode in scope this release) */
--surface-primary:   #FFFFFF;
--surface-secondary: #F5F5F5;
--surface-elevated:  #FAFAFA;
--border:             #E0E0E0;
--text-primary:      #212121;
--text-secondary:    #616161;
--text-disabled:     #9E9E9E;

/* Dark mode (reserved, not built this release) */
--surface-primary-dark:   #121212;
--surface-secondary-dark: #1E1E1E;
--surface-elevated-dark:  #242424;
--border-dark:            #303030;
--text-primary-dark:      #EEEEEE;
--text-secondary-dark:    #9E9E9E;

/* ── Status / Staleness ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
--stale-banner:      #795548;   /* Brown — pipeline overdue */
--storm-mode:        #4A148C;   /* Purple — storm mode active */

/* ── Typography ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
--font-primary: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
```

## B7. User Journey

Emotional arc, primary flow (citizen driver, Search → Get Directions → Route Detail → Start), applying REQ-RTE-003's non-alarmist tone throughout:

| STEP | USER DOES | USER FEELS | PLAN SPECIFIES? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Land on Home | Opens app, sees map + search pill | Orientation | REQ-MAP-001, REQ-SRCH-002 |
| 2. Search / pick origin & destination | Types a place or taps the map | Control | REQ-SRCH-002/004, REQ-SRCH-001 fallback, loading spinner |
| 3. See route colors (critical trust moment) | Scans cards' green/amber/red/blue borders | Panic-vs-confidence gets decided here — must read as informative, not alarming | REQ-RTE-002, REQ-RTE-003, draining signals hope not just danger |
| 4. Route Detail + Start | Scans turn-by-turn + forecast chart, taps Start | Confidence to act | REQ-DET-001/003/004, REQ-RTE-005 |

## B8. Frontend-Specific Constraints

- Reuses the existing floodmap-backend (Valhalla 3.6.2) as-is — this document does not redefine backend API contracts beyond what Part A already specifies.
- Scope limited to wireframe 2a — 1a/1b/1c out of scope.
- Frontend framework decision (refactor vanilla-JS `app.js` in place vs. React rewrite) intentionally undecided by request; no build tooling exists today (static files served by nginx), which favors refactor-in-place if revisited.
- No public-facing deployment planned.
- Geocoding (REQ-SRCH-002) depends on a Photon instance not yet provisioned.
- QA scoped against the existing bundled sample dataset rather than new fixtures.
- Dark mode explicitly out of scope this release.
- **Sequencing gate:** REQ-MAP-002/003/004, REQ-DET-001, REQ-MAP-005, and REQ-RTE-002's draining flag can be built against a mocked API in parallel with backend work, but cannot be integration-tested until Part A's PR3 lands (T8, T16, T17, T18). Most of Part B's acceptance criteria are unverifiable until then.

- Design tokens (§B6) merged in, with `--seg-*`/`--depth-*` usage clarified across all routing UI.
- Backend costing model extension for Sedan/SUV (Part A T16).

## B11. Frontend Test Plan

New pure-function logic, following the existing repo convention (`tests/test_point_depth.js` using `node:test` against pure exports from `frontend/point_depth.js`). DOM-heavy flows have no test harness in this repo (no jsdom/E2E) and this plan doesn't introduce one — those stay manual-QA per their own acceptance criteria.

```
CODE PATHS (new pure functions)                         COVERAGE
[+] frontend/depth_scale.js (new)
  └── bucketDepthCm(depthCm) → --depth-* token
      ├── 0-20cm, 20-40cm, ..., >100cm (6 bands)         → depth_scale.test.js
      ├── boundary values: exactly 20/40/60/80/100       → depth_scale.test.js
      └── no-data/undefined → --depth-unknown             → depth_scale.test.js
[+] frontend/route_status.js (new)
  └── classifySegment(depthCm, thresholdCm, drainingFlag) → --seg-* token
      ├── < 70% threshold → passable                     → route_status.test.js
      ├── 70-100% threshold → pre-closure                 → route_status.test.js
      ├── boundary: exactly 70%, exactly 100%             → route_status.test.js
      ├── >= 100% threshold → impassable                   → route_status.test.js
      ├── drainingFlag=true + not impassable → draining (reads flag, does not re-derive)  → route_status.test.js
      └── drainingFlag=true + impassable → stays impassable (defensive guard)             → route_status.test.js
[+] frontend/staleness.js (new)
  └── isStale(lastUpdateTs, now, overdueThresholdMs) → boolean
      ├── below threshold → false                         → staleness.test.js
      ├── at/above threshold → true                        → staleness.test.js
      └── boundary: exactly at threshold                   → staleness.test.js
[+] forecast-chart bar-building logic (REQ-DET-001)
      └── requested timestep missing (post-drainage-stop gap) → reuse last-known + --stale-banner → forecast_chart.test.js

QUALITY TARGET: ★★★ (behavior + boundary + edge) for all modules — these are
safety-classification functions; boundary values ARE the primary risk, not edge cases.
```

**Test files:**
1. `tests/depth_scale.test.js` — one case per §B6 band, the 5 exact cm boundaries, undefined/null → `--depth-unknown`.
2. `tests/route_status.test.js` — passable/pre-closure/impassable happy paths (API-supplied threshold), 70%/100% boundaries, `drainingFlag=true` on passable/pre-closure → draining, defensive `drainingFlag=true` + impassable → stays impassable.
3. `tests/staleness.test.js` — below/at/above the overdue threshold.
4. `tests/forecast_chart.test.js` — missing timestep → last-known value + `--stale-banner`, not a false zero or a crash.

All P1 — gate the same safety-critical logic REQ-RTE-002/REQ-MAP-004 depend on.

## B12. Frontend Failure Modes

| New codepath | Realistic failure | Test? | Error handling? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Route calc request (REQ-RTE-001) | Backend timeout/5xx | Covered by §B5 error treatment | "Couldn't calculate a route — try again" + Retry | Clear, recoverable |
| Photon search (REQ-SRCH-002) | Geocoder down/slow | N/A (degrade path) | Degrades to map-click | Clear, no dead end |
| Forecast chart -30 bar (REQ-DET-001) | Requested cycle missing (drainage-confirmed stop) | Yes — `forecast_chart.test.js` | Reuse last-known + `--stale-banner` | Clear (stale, not silently wrong) |
| `draining` flag (Part A T18) | Backend sets `draining:true` on an impassable segment | Yes — `route_status.test.js`'s defensive case | Frontend guards it | Correct even if backend misbehaves |
| Tile endpoint (Part A T17) | Tile server down/slow | Backend-side fallback, no frontend branch to test | Falls back to last-good tile set | Map stays usable |

All identified failure modes have a test and/or explicit error handling — no open critical gaps.

## Cross-Cutting: Overall Worktree Parallelization

| Lane | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Lane 1 | Backend PR1 (T4, T12-T15, E2) | — |
| Lane 2 | Backend PR2 (T1, T5, T6, T9, E3/E4) | Lane 1 merged (needs `db_config.py`) |
| Lane 3 | Backend PR3 (T7, T8, T10, E5/E6) → T16 → T17 → T18 | Lane 2 merged (needs T6 schema) |
| Lane 4 | Frontend T1-T8, T11 (build + unit tests against mocks) | Independent — can start immediately |
| Lane 5 | Frontend T9, T10 (real-data integration) | Lane 3's T16/T18 deployed |

Lanes 1-3 are strictly sequential (each PR's DB layer depends on the prior PR's schema). Lane 4 runs fully in parallel with Lanes 1-3. Lane 5 is a ~15-minute tail once Lane 3 finishes.

**Effort estimate (backend critical path T5→T6→T8→T16→T17→T18):** ~8-9 human-days / ~2 CC-days on the critical path; ~13.5 human-days / ~3.25 CC-days for the full backend task list including parallel-safe items. Frontend build effort (T1-T8, T11) is ~3.3 human-hours / ~1 CC-hour, almost entirely parallelizable with the backend critical path.
